chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Shaybani, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Yunus ibn Zabyan! Convey to Atiyya from me that whoever drinks a gulp of wine, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, curses him, and His Angels, and His Messengers, and the Believers. So if he drinks it until he becomes intoxicated from it, the Spirit of Faith is removed from his body, and a stupid, malicious, Accursed spirit rides in him, so he neglects the Prayer. So when he neglects the Prayer, the Angels rebuke him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to him: 'My servant! You have disbelieved,' and the Angels have rebuked you with a disgrace for you, 'My servant!'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A disgrace, a disgrace, just as the disgrace is. And by Allah, the rebuke of the Sublime, Majestic is His Name, for one hour is more severe than the punishment of a thousand years.'
He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Accursed, wherever they are found, they are seized and killed with a fierce killing.'

Then he said: 'O Yunus! Accursed, accursed is the one who neglects the Command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If he takes to the land, He ravages him, and if he takes to the sea, He drowns him. He is angered for the anger of the Sublime, Mighty is His Name.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical consequences of drinking wine according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the progressive spiritual decay of the wine drinker, where a single gulp invites a universal curse, while intoxication expels the spirit of faith for a base one, leading to the abandonment of prayer. This neglect triggers a severe divine rebuke, with the Imam emphasizing that the shame of the Great One for just one hour is more intense than a thousand years of punishment. The narration concludes by affirming the cursed status of those who neglect God's command, promising destruction whether they are on land or sea, as God is angered for His own sake.
